time.desc: One party disclosed that it had submitted a formal written response to multiple ceasefire conditions proposed by its opponent, marking a new stage of ceasefire negotiations.
One of the warring parties and its allies launched a joint attack on facilities near key sea lanes, causing casualties. The fighting spilled over to shipping points.

Major countries outside the region have jointly proposed a multi-point plan that includes a ceasefire and the restoration of access to key sea lanes, forming a mediation path that is different from the previous ceasefire framework.

In a national address, the top leaders of the warring parties announced that they will escalate severe attacks on their opponents in the coming weeks and set a time target for ending the conflict as soon as possible.

The leaders of the warring parties publicly threatened to attack the opponent's critical civilian infrastructure, and then the opponent's senior officials warned of counterattack by possibly blocking another important sea channel.
One side announced a suspension of bombings and attacks against its opponents and set up a ceasefire window for several weeks. Market expectations for conflict risks have significantly cooled.
One ally publicly stated that the ceasefire arrangement did not restrict its actions against third-party armed forces, triggering disputes over the scope and sustainability of the ceasefire.
Opponents proposed the idea of ​​charging fees for passage of key sea lanes, triggering legal debates and the game over passage rules heating up.

The military of one party officially launched a naval blockade of the opponent's port and stated that it would not affect the navigation of ships in non-opponent ports. Since then, the prospect of a ceasefire has become unclear again.

The leader of one of the parties involved in the war publicly called on all countries to go to the key strait to rush to transport oil, claiming that the opponent had been basically defeated, and related oil prices rose sharply late at night.

The navy of one of the participating parties began to mobilize troops to key straits and prepare to blockade the opponent's ports. The actions were carried out at the same time as the talks between the two sides.
